clues: This city stands on a wide river in the northeastern part of its plains state.
Summers here are hot and a bit humid, with about 50 afternoons a year over 90 degrees. Winters are cool to cold and fairly dry.
This town was picked as the capital when the land was not yet a state. Charles Robinson was its first governor.
The Brown court case bears this town's name in its title. It struck down school rules that split kids by race.
The governor of Kansas works in this city. State lawmakers meet here in the state capitol.
